reasoning: The failing assertion is a single, unretried raw fetch of a live p2p preview URL (pageB.request.get(previewSrc, { failOnStatusCode: false })), which returned 502. The 502 is produced by the preview proxy route (routes/sharing.py → sharing_device_preview) when service.pull_preview.send raises CallError/P2PServiceError. That call uses a fresh QUIC socket with LAN_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1.5s and, on timeout, falls back to the deliberately unreachable hub (ws://127.0.0.1:9), yielding the 502. This is a transient network timeout, not a broken feature: the app itself documents this exact failure mode in static/sharing/remote_gallery.js ('native lazy-loading easily has dozens in flight — enough to trip call timeouts ... which surfaced as 502s') and mitigates it with bounded concurrency plus a single delayed retry. The test bypasses that mitigation by firing its own extra unretried request concurrently with the browser's queued preview loading. The application is otherwise healthy: A's log shows no preview-generation error, list_files/list_shared/pull operations all succeed, and the remaining 11 tests (including later gallery/pull scenarios) passed. Test history also shows the flakiness signature rather than a regression: three runs each failed a DIFFERENT test (revoke_a_device net::ERR_ABORTED twice — a real race now fixed in the current code via waitForURL — and this preview 502 once), with 11/12 passing each time.

suggestedAction: Treat as flaky and harden the preview assertion instead of changing application code: wait for the first .remote-photo-card img to actually load successfully (e.g., dataset.previewState === 'done' or naturalWidth > 0), which exercises the app's own concurrency limit and retry, or wrap the raw preview fetch in a short retry loop (retry up to ~2-3 times with a small delay) before asserting a 2xx status. Re-running the ordered suite against a fresh two-instance sandbox is also expected to pass.
